result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name all four problem behaviors and propose autosave, removing the unit confirmation, safer reset, and regrouping. B is stronger on defaults: it suggests copying settings from another hive, and it adds a status line on the hive screen. A is clearly better on honesty: it says it is assuming settings is behind the reviews, checks existing reviews and analytics, and lists metrics to watch in a staged rollout. B's checks all happen before release and say little about what to watch afterward. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the same four problem behaviors and propose similar fixes: autosave, no confirmation on the unit change, recommended alerts on for new hives, and the reset moved to Advanced. A is slightly stronger on defaults because it offers copying settings from an existing hive and a recoverable undo toast for reset. B is clearly stronger on working without user testing: it says outright that it hasn't seen the reviews, and it lists specific checks (tagging the reviews, analytics on the discard popup and on hives with zero alerts, a staged rollout watching mute rate and support contacts), where A only has pre-release walkthroughs.
